metadata.course: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence
metadata.attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
metadata.scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
metadata.description: A full-year Earth Science course: the practices and reference tools of the discipline, Earth's interior and plate tectonics, minerals, rocks and the rock cycle, volcanoes, earthquakes and crustal deformation, geologic time and Earth history, weathering, streams and groundwater, oceans, coasts and glaciers, the atmosphere, weather and climate, resources, hazards and sustainability, and Earth's place in the solar system.

id_namespace.reason: Concept ids are global; the prefix keeps this course disjoint from the shipped courses that share concept titles.

concepts.title: Air and Water Pollution Chemistry
concepts.summary: Ground-level ozone forms when sunlight acts on nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons, acid deposition forms when sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides dissolve in precipitation, and nutrient runoff fuels blooms that consume oxygen, so each problem has its own chemistry and its own remedy.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Air Masses and Their Source Regions
concepts.summary: An air mass takes the temperature and moisture of the surface it forms over, so a continental polar mass brings cold dry air and a maritime tropical mass brings warm humid air, and its two-letter name records both qualities.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Angle of Insolation and Day Length
concepts.summary: Insolation intensity varies with the sine of the Sun's angle above the horizon, so a low winter Sun spreads the same energy over a longer path and a larger area, and beyond the polar circles the day length reaches 24 hours or zero.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Aquifers, Wells, and Overdraft
concepts.summary: A pumped well draws down a cone of depression whose shape depends on permeability, and pumping faster than recharge lowers the regional water table, dries shallow wells and can draw salt water inland at a coast.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Chemical and Biochemical Sedimentary Rocks
concepts.strand: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.unit: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.summary: Evaporites such as halite and gypsum form where dissolved ions concentrate as water evaporates, while limestone forms from calcium carbonate shells or by direct precipitation, so each records a water chemistry rather than a current.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Choosing a Display for Earth Data
concepts.strand: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.unit: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.summary: Categories are compared with a bar chart, a quantity tracked through time is plotted as a line, and two measured variables are plotted against each other as a scatter, so a mismatched display hides the pattern the data actually contain.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Climate Controls and Regional Differences
concepts.summary: Climate is the long-term statistics of weather and its controls are latitude, altitude, distance from water, ocean currents, prevailing wind and topography, so two places at the same latitude can have different climates.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Climate Decides Which Weathering Dominates
concepts.summary: Warm wet climates favour chemical weathering and produce clay-rich soil on rounded slopes, while cold or dry climates favour mechanical breakdown and leave angular debris under thin soil.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Climate Shapes the Landscape
concepts.summary: Humid landscapes are rounded with thick soil and an integrated drainage network, while arid landscapes are angular with thin regolith and internal drainage, so climate can be read from the shape of the land.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Compositional Layers and the Lithosphere
concepts.summary: Earth is divided by composition into crust, mantle and core and by strength into a rigid lithosphere over a weak asthenosphere, so the lithosphere is crust plus uppermost mantle rather than crust alone, and it is the layer that moves as a plate.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Contact and Regional Metamorphism
concepts.strand: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.unit: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.summary: Heat from an intrusion bakes a narrow aureole of non-foliated rock such as hornfels, whereas directed pressure across a convergent margin produces foliated rock over a belt hundreds of kilometres wide.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Continental Drift and the Missing Mechanism
concepts.summary: Wegener matched coastlines, fossils and rock sequences across the Atlantic but could name no force able to move a continent, so the idea waited until seafloor spreading supplied a mechanism, which shows that a correct pattern still needs a physical process before it is accepted.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Contour Lines, Relief, and Profiles
concepts.strand: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.unit: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.summary: Contour lines join points of equal elevation, so closely spaced lines mark a steep slope, hachured contours mark a depression, and a contour bending upstream marks a valley floor.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Convergent Boundaries: Subduction and Collision
concepts.summary: Where an oceanic plate meets another plate it subducts and produces a trench with a volcanic arc behind it, while where two continents collide neither subducts and the crust thickens into fold mountains such as the Himalaya.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Cooling Rate Sets Texture
concepts.strand: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.unit: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.summary: Slow cooling at depth grows large interlocking crystals in an intrusive rock while rapid cooling at the surface gives fine grains or glass, so texture records the cooling history of a rock rather than its composition.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Criteria and Constraints in Earth Engineering
concepts.summary: A design is judged against criteria such as safety and cost while constrained by budget, materials, regulation and site conditions, so a solution is optimal only for the constraints it was designed under.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Cross-Cutting Relationships and Inclusions
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.summary: A fault, intrusion or erosion surface is younger than the rock it cuts, and a fragment enclosed in another rock is older than its host, so these relations order events without any date at all.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Cycles, Trends, and Data Reliability
concepts.strand: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.unit: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.summary: Many Earth records cycle on daily, seasonal or tidal periods, so a trend can be read only after averaging across at least one full cycle, and a conclusion drawn from a few scattered measurements stays provisional until more samples agree.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Depositional Glacial Landforms
concepts.summary: Ice drops unsorted till as moraines and drumlins while meltwater carries sorted sand and gravel into outwash and eskers, so sorting separates ice-laid from water-laid sediment.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Deserts, Alluvial Fans, and Playas
concepts.summary: An arid basin collects coarse sediment in an alluvial fan at the mountain front and dissolved salts in a playa at its centre, so internal drainage concentrates minerals instead of carrying them to the sea.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Dew Point, Humidity, and Cloud Formation
concepts.summary: Relative humidity compares the vapour present with the maximum the air can hold at that temperature, so rising air cools to its dew point and condenses cloud at the lifting condensation level.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Diagnostic Properties and Mineral Formation
concepts.strand: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.unit: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.summary: Hardness, cleavage, streak and luster identify a mineral because each reflects its composition and structure, and a mineral forms by crystallising from melt, precipitating from solution or recrystallising under heat and pressure.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Divergent Boundaries and Rift Valleys
concepts.summary: Where plates move apart, magma rises to build a mid-ocean ridge with shallow earthquakes and basaltic lava, and the same process inside a continent splits it into a rift valley such as the East African Rift.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Earth System Feedbacks Amplify or Damp Change
concepts.summary: Melting ice lowering albedo, thawing permafrost releasing carbon and warmer air holding more water vapour are positive feedbacks, while increased weathering and ocean uptake are negative ones, so the net response depends on which balance wins and over what timescale.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Energy Density, Capacity Factor, and the Grid
concepts.summary: A fuel stores far more energy per kilogram than a battery and a wind or solar plant produces at a low capacity factor, so replacing firm generation needs storage or backup rather than nameplate capacity alone.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Erosional Glacial Landforms
concepts.summary: Ice widens a stream-cut V into a U-shaped valley, scoops cirques and horns at its head and scratches the bedrock beneath it, so striations and their orientation record the path the ice followed.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Evidence for an Expanding Universe
concepts.summary: Distant galaxies show redshifts proportional to their distance, the cosmic microwave background is a relic of a hot dense early state and the measured hydrogen and helium abundances match prediction, so the three together support a hot Big Bang.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Flood Frequency and Land-Use Effects
concepts.summary: A 100-year flood has a one percent chance in any year rather than arriving once a century, and paving a watershed raises peak discharge because rain runs off instead of soaking in.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Focus, Epicenter, and Wave Order
concepts.summary: The focus is where rupture begins underground and the epicenter is the point on the surface above it, and because P waves are fastest and surface waves slowest a station records P before S before the surface waves that do most of the damage.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Formation and Differentiation of the Solar System
concepts.summary: The solar nebula flattened into a disk in which dust accreted into planetesimals that separated by density, so rocky planets formed where the disk was hot and ice-rich giant planets formed beyond the frost line.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Fossil Fuel Formation and Trapping
concepts.summary: Coal forms from compressed swamp vegetation while oil and gas form from marine organic matter buried in a source rock, then migrate into a porous reservoir sealed by a trap, so a field needs all three elements present.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: From Weathering to Lithification
concepts.strand: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.unit: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.summary: A clastic rock forms by weathering, transport, deposition and then compaction and cementation, so grain rounding and sorting record how far the sediment travelled and by which agent rather than how old it is.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Fronts, Cyclones, and Forecast Confidence
concepts.summary: A cold front advances steeply and produces a short band of heavy rain followed by clearing, a warm front slopes gently and produces long light precipitation, and forecast confidence falls with lead time as model solutions diverge.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Galaxies and the Scale of the Universe
concepts.summary: A galaxy is a gravitationally bound system of stars, gas and dark matter, and because the Milky Way is about 100,000 light years across while Andromeda lies 2.5 million light years away, the spacing between galaxies far exceeds their size.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Glacier Mass Balance and Flow
concepts.summary: A glacier advances when accumulation exceeds ablation and retreats when ablation exceeds accumulation, and it flows by internal deformation plus basal sliding, so terminus position records mass balance rather than temperature alone.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: GPS, Earthquake Belts, and Paleoclimate Clues
concepts.summary: Satellite geodesy measures plate motion directly at a few centimetres per year, earthquakes concentrate in narrow belts rather than at random, and glacial deposits now in tropical latitudes mark continents that have drifted.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Gradient, Rate of Change, and Density
concepts.strand: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.unit: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.topic: Reference Tables, Units, and Formula Tools
concepts.summary: Gradient is the change in a field value divided by distance, rate of change is change divided by time and density is mass divided by volume, so each result carries combined units such as metres per kilometre or grams per cubic centimetre rather than a bare number.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Hazard Maps Follow Plate Boundaries
concepts.summary: Subduction zones concentrate the largest earthquakes, tsunamis and explosive volcanoes, transform boundaries concentrate shallow earthquakes, and stable interiors produce few of either, so a hazard map is drawn along the boundaries.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Heat Flow, Gravity, and the Geodynamo
concepts.summary: Heat flow is highest at mid-ocean ridges and lowest over old continental interiors, and the magnetic field is generated by convection in the liquid outer core, so heat flow, gravity and magnetism together constrain any model of the interior.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Heat, Pressure, and Foliation
concepts.strand: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.unit: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.summary: Directed pressure at depth aligns platy minerals perpendicular to the stress, so increasing metamorphic grade turns shale into slate, phyllite, schist and gneiss, and the foliation records the direction of that pressure.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Hot Spots and Plate Motion Records
concepts.summary: A mantle plume stays roughly fixed while the plate rides over it, so the plume builds a chain of progressively older volcanoes, and the bend in the Hawaiian-Emperor chain records a change in the direction of Pacific motion.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Hypotheses, Models, and Testable Predictions
concepts.strand: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.unit: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.summary: A hypothesis is an explanation phrased so that a prediction follows from it, and because most Earth processes cannot be run as a laboratory experiment the hypothesis is tested by comparing a model's prediction with field data such as measured plate motion.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Ice-Albedo Feedback
concepts.summary: Snow and ice reflect most incoming sunlight while open ocean absorbs most of it, so melting ice exposes a darker surface that absorbs more energy and drives further warming.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Impervious Surfaces and the Urban Water Cycle
concepts.summary: Paving and compaction replace infiltration with runoff, so a city sends a larger and faster flood peak into its streams, recharges less groundwater and runs warmer than the surrounding countryside.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Index Fossils Date a Bed
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.summary: A useful index fossil had a wide geographic range, a short time span and a recognisable form, so its presence pins a bed to a narrow interval while a long-ranging fossil such as a shark tooth cannot.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Karst, Caves, and Sinkholes
concepts.summary: Carbonic acid dissolves limestone along joints into caves, sinkholes and streams that vanish underground, so a falling water table can leave a cave roof unsupported beneath a road.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Kepler's Laws and Orbital Speed
concepts.summary: Each planet follows an ellipse with the Sun at one focus and sweeps equal areas in equal times, so it moves fastest at perihelion, and the square of its orbital period is proportional to the cube of its semi-major axis.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Lateral Continuity and Correlation
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.summary: A layer extends sideways until its environment ends, so separated outcrops are correlated by matching rock type, stacking order and fossil content rather than by distance alone.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Latitude, Longitude, and Map Position
concepts.strand: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.unit: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.summary: Latitude is measured north or south of the equator from 0 to 90 degrees and longitude east or west of the prime meridian from 0 to 180, and because meridians converge at the poles a degree of longitude narrows from about 111 kilometres at the equator to zero at the poles.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Latitudinal Energy Imbalance
concepts.summary: The tropics absorb more solar energy than they emit while the poles emit more than they absorb, and winds and currents carry the surplus poleward, so the imbalance rather than the global average drives circulation.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Layers and the Temperature Profile
concepts.summary: Temperature falls with height through the troposphere because that layer is heated from below, and rises through the stratosphere because ozone absorbs ultraviolet light, and that inversion traps weather in the lower layer.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Life Alters the Earth System
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.topic: Earth History, Life, and System Change
concepts.summary: Organisms build reefs and shells, bury carbon and release oxygen, so the biosphere has changed the atmosphere and the rock record and the two have co-evolved rather than life merely adapting to a fixed planet.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Magma Composition Sets Eruption Style
concepts.strand: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.unit: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.summary: High-silica magma is viscous and traps gas so it erupts explosively, while low-silica basaltic magma flows easily and erupts quietly, so silica content rather than temperature decides the style of an eruption.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Magnitude, Intensity, and Site Effects
concepts.summary: Magnitude measures energy released on a logarithmic scale where one unit is about 32 times more energy while intensity measures shaking and damage at a place, and soft saturated sediment amplifies shaking and can liquefy.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Mantle Convection and Slab Pull
concepts.summary: Convection in the mantle supplies the motion, but the dominant force is slab pull, in which cold dense subducting lithosphere sinks and drags the rest of the plate with it, with ridge push a smaller contribution.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Mass Extinctions and Their Drivers
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.topic: Earth History, Life, and System Change
concepts.summary: The end-Permian extinction removed about 90 percent of marine species alongside the Siberian Traps eruptions and the end-Cretaceous extinction coincides with an iridium layer and the Chicxulub impact, so each extinction pairs a kill mechanism with a dated cause.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Matching the Isotope to the Material
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.summary: Carbon-14 with a 5,730-year half-life dates organic material only to about 50,000 years while potassium-argon and uranium-lead date volcanic and crystalline rock over millions to billions of years, so the wrong isotope gives no usable age.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Meanders, Floodplains, and Deltas
concepts.summary: A stream erodes the outer bank of a bend and deposits a point bar on the inner bank, so meanders migrate and may be cut off as oxbows, while a delta builds where the stream enters standing water and drops its load.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Measuring Temperature, Pressure, and Humidity
concepts.summary: A barometer measures pressure, a psychrometer compares wet and dry bulb readings to give relative humidity and dew point, and an anemometer measures wind speed, and a station model packs all of them into one symbol.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Mechanical and Chemical Weathering
concepts.summary: Mechanical weathering breaks rock without altering its minerals through frost wedging, unloading and abrasion, while chemical weathering alters them by hydrolysis, oxidation and carbonation, and each exposes fresh surface that speeds the other.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Milankovitch Cycles and Ice Ages
concepts.summary: Variations in orbital eccentricity over about 100,000 years, axial tilt over 41,000 and precession over 23,000 change how sunlight is distributed by season at high northern latitudes, which paces glacial and interglacial cycles.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Mitigation, Adaptation, and Decisions under Uncertainty
concepts.summary: Mitigation reduces the forcing while adaptation reduces vulnerability to the change already committed, and because projections are scenarios rather than forecasts, planning weighs outcomes across a range of them.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Monitoring Gives Warning, Not Certainty
concepts.summary: Rising seismicity, ground deformation and gas emission precede most eruptions, so a monitored volcano can be warned on a scale of days to weeks even though the exact onset cannot be predicted.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Mountain Belts, Isostasy, and Rebound
concepts.summary: Collision thickens the crust so that it floats higher on the mantle, and because the crust stays in isostatic balance, removing mass by erosion lets the remaining rock rise.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Natural and Human Forcing
concepts.summary: Solar variation, volcanic aerosols and orbital cycles are natural forcings while greenhouse gases, aerosols and land use are human ones, and a human cause is confirmed when the observed pattern, such as stratospheric cooling with surface warming, matches its signature.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: New York's Bedrock Records Three Orogenies
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.topic: New York and Regional Geologic History
concepts.summary: Grenville metamorphism about 1.1 billion years ago built the Adirondack basement, and the Taconic, Acadian and Alleghenian collisions then deformed the eastern bedrock of the state in succession.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Observation, Inference, and Explanation
concepts.strand: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.unit: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.summary: An observation is what an instrument or a sense directly detects while an inference is an explanation built from it, so a statement about why a layer formed is an inference and must be checked against evidence other than the layer itself.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Outgassing, Oceans, and the Rise of Oxygen
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.topic: Earth History, Life, and System Change
concepts.summary: Volcanic outgassing supplied the early atmosphere and condensing water vapour formed the oceans, and photosynthesis later raised oxygen enough to oxidise iron, which is why banded iron formations lie beneath the red beds.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Paleozoic Seas and the Catskill Delta
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.topic: New York and Regional Geologic History
concepts.summary: Shallow Paleozoic seas across New York deposited limestone and shale with marine fossils, and erosion of the Acadian mountains built the Catskill delta, so the state's strata record a shoreline that shifted back and forth.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Phases and Eclipses from Orbital Geometry
concepts.summary: The Moon's phase depends on how much of its sunlit half faces Earth over a cycle of about 29.5 days, and a solar eclipse occurs only at new moon and a lunar eclipse only at full moon when the tilted orbit crosses the ecliptic.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Pleistocene Ice Shaped the Present Surface
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.topic: New York and Regional Geologic History
concepts.summary: The Laurentide ice sheet retreated about 20,000 years ago leaving drumlins, moraines, erratics and the over-deepened Finger Lakes, so most New York landforms are far younger than the bedrock beneath them.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Porosity, Permeability, and the Water Table
concepts.summary: Porosity is the fraction of void space while permeability is how well those voids connect, so clay can be porous yet hold water instead of yielding it, and the water table is the top of the saturated zone.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Pressure Gradients and Wind
concepts.summary: Air accelerates from high toward low pressure, is deflected to the right in the Northern Hemisphere by the Coriolis effect, and crosses isobars at an angle near the surface because friction slows it.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Proxies Extend the Climate Record
concepts.summary: Ice cores preserve trapped air and oxygen isotopes, tree rings record growth year by year and sediments preserve microfossils, so proxies reach beyond the instrumental record although each has its own dating limits.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Pyroclastic Flows, Ash, and Lahar Hazards
concepts.summary: A pyroclastic flow of hot gas and ash can outrun a car while falling ash collapses roofs and shuts airspace, so most volcanic deaths come from flows, blasts and lahars rather than from lava.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Radioactive Decay and Half-Life
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.summary: A radioactive parent decays at a fixed rate, so after one half-life half the parent remains and after two a quarter, and the parent-to-daughter ratio dates a sample only if the system stayed closed to gain or loss.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Reading Folds and Faults
concepts.summary: An anticline arches with the oldest beds in its core and a syncline troughs with the youngest in its core, while a normal fault drops its hanging wall under tension and a reverse fault raises it under compression.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Reading the Earth Science Reference Tables
concepts.strand: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.unit: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.topic: Reference Tables, Units, and Formula Tools
concepts.summary: The reference tables collect the constants, mineral and rock properties and chart scales used throughout the course, so a value must be taken from the correct row and kept with its stated unit, because density for example is listed in grams per cubic centimetre.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Recurrence Intervals and Probability
concepts.summary: A recurrence interval is the average interval between events of a given size, so a 50-year flood has a two percent chance in any year and two of them can still occur in consecutive years.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Redshift Is Expansion, Not Motion
concepts.summary: Cosmological redshift grows with distance because space stretches the wavelength in transit, so a distant galaxy is not travelling through space at the speed its redshift implies but is carried by the expansion between it and us.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Renewable, Nonrenewable, and Reserves
concepts.summary: A renewable resource regenerates within a human lifetime and a nonrenewable one does not, while a reserve is the part of a resource that is known and economically recoverable, so a reserve can grow with price or technology and no new discovery.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Risk Is Not the Same as Hazard
concepts.summary: Risk combines the probability of a hazard with the exposure and vulnerability of what lies in its path, so an earthquake of one magnitude carries far greater risk where buildings are unreinforced.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Rock Assemblage Indicates a Past Setting
concepts.strand: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.unit: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.topic: Rock Cycle and Earth Materials Synthesis
concepts.summary: A limestone with marine shells records a warm shallow sea, a basalt flow records volcanism and a conglomerate of rounded pebbles records a nearby highland, so several rock types read together reconstruct a setting.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Runoff, Infiltration, and Watershed Response
concepts.summary: Infiltration depends on soil texture, vegetation, slope and rainfall intensity, so a compacted or saturated surface turns rain into flash runoff that a porous forest soil would have absorbed.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Salinity and Density Structure
concepts.summary: Seawater averages about 35 parts per thousand of dissolved salt and grows denser as it becomes colder or saltier, so cold polar water sinks beneath warmer water and the ocean stratifies by density.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Scale, Rate, and the Geologic Record
concepts.strand: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.unit: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.summary: Earth processes run at rates from millimetres per year to minutes, so a canyon cut over millions of years and a flood that moves its sediment in a day are successive chapters of one landscape history rather than opposites.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Sea Level Change and Coastal Response
concepts.summary: Eustatic sea level rises with melting land ice and warming water while isostatic change moves the land itself, so a subsiding coast drowns its river valleys while a rebounding coast exposes raised beaches.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Seafloor Provinces
concepts.summary: A continental margin runs from shelf through slope and rise to the abyssal plain, and a passive margin carries a wide shelf while an active margin has a narrow shelf and a trench, so basin shape records the plate setting.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Seafloor Spreading and Magnetic Stripes
concepts.summary: New oceanic crust forms at a ridge and records the field polarity as it cools, so the symmetrical stripes of alternating polarity on either side of the ridge record reversals and show that the ocean floor grows outward from the axis.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Sedimentary Structures Record Environments
concepts.strand: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.unit: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.summary: Cross-beds record migrating ripples, mudcracks record wetting and drying of exposed mud and a graded bed records a waning current, so structures identify the setting where grain size alone cannot.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Seismic Waves as Probes of the Interior
concepts.summary: P waves travel through solids, liquids and gases while S waves travel only through solids, so the S-wave shadow zone beyond about 103 degrees from an epicenter shows that the outer core is liquid.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Shield, Cinder Cone, and Composite Volcanoes
concepts.summary: Low-viscosity basalt builds a broad shield, short gas-rich bursts build a steep cinder cone, and alternating ash and viscous lava above a subduction zone build a composite cone, so shape records the magma and the setting.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Silicate Structure Sets Hardness and Cleavage
concepts.strand: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.unit: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.summary: Every silicate is built from SiO4 tetrahedra, and the way those tetrahedra link decides cleavage, so isolated tetrahedra in olivine give no cleavage while sheets in mica split into thin flat flakes.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Soil Horizons and Formation
concepts.summary: Soil is weathered mineral matter mixed with organic matter, water and air and developed into O, A, B and C horizons, and its depth and fertility depend on climate, parent material, slope and the time it has had to form.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Star Formation and the Main Sequence
concepts.summary: A collapsing cloud of gas and dust heats until hydrogen fusion begins and outward pressure balances gravity, and because a more massive star fuses far faster it is brighter but lives a shorter life.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Stellar Evolution and Element Synthesis
concepts.summary: A low-mass star ends as a white dwarf after shedding a planetary nebula while a high-mass star ends in a supernova that leaves a neutron star or black hole, and the heavy elements of Earth were forged in such stars and dispersed by supernovae.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Stream Work along a Profile
concepts.summary: A stream erodes where it is steep and fast, carries its load and deposits where velocity falls, so a graded stream adjusts its slope until erosion and deposition balance toward base level.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Stress, Strain, and Brittle or Ductile Response
concepts.summary: Compression shortens rock, tension stretches it and shear twists it, and the same rock fractures under shallow cold conditions but folds under deep hot ones, so a structure records depth as well as force.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Structural and Nonstructural Mitigation
concepts.summary: A levee, retaining wall or seismic brace reduces damage directly while zoning, insurance and evacuation reduce exposure, and a levee can raise risk when it encourages building behind it and then fails.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Superposition and Original Horizontality
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.summary: In an undisturbed sequence each layer is older than the one above it, and because sediment settles horizontally, tilted or folded layers must have been disturbed after they were deposited.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Surface Currents and Gyres
concepts.summary: Prevailing winds plus the Coriolis effect drive large circular gyres with narrow fast western boundary currents such as the Gulf Stream and broad slow eastern currents, so surface circulation carries heat poleward.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Sustainability as Living Within Regeneration Rates
concepts.summary: A use is sustainable only if renewable resources are consumed no faster than they regenerate and wastes are released no faster than they are absorbed, so a fishery can last only up to its maximum sustainable yield.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Tectonics and Water Drive the Rock Cycle
concepts.strand: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.unit: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.topic: Rock Cycle and Earth Materials Synthesis
concepts.summary: Melting, metamorphism and uplift are supplied by plate tectonics while weathering and erosion are supplied by the water cycle, so a rock converts into another type only through one of those processes acting on it.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Tectonics Controls Topography and Climate
concepts.summary: Uplift builds mountains that cast a rain shadow and expose fresh silicate rock to weathering, and silicate weathering consumes carbon dioxide, so tectonic uplift can cool global climate over millions of years.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: The Four Spheres and Their Exchange at Boundaries
concepts.strand: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.unit: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.summary: The geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere exchange matter and energy across their boundaries, so a volcanic eruption moves gases and ash from the geosphere into the atmosphere and can cool climate for a year or more.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: The Geologic Time Scale
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.summary: Eons, eras, periods and epochs are defined by major changes in the fossil record, and the Precambrian covers roughly seven-eighths of Earth history, so the scale divides time by events rather than into equal parts.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: The Greenhouse Effect
concepts.summary: Greenhouse gases absorb outgoing infrared radiation and re-emit part of it downward, so without them the surface would average about 18 degrees below zero Celsius instead of its present value.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: The Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram
concepts.summary: The H-R diagram plots luminosity against surface temperature, and its main sequence, giants and white dwarfs occupy separate regions, so a star's position identifies its stage and relative size.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: The Ocean's Salt Budget
concepts.summary: Rivers deliver dissolved ions from weathering while evaporation removes water and hydrothermal circulation and sediment trap ions, so ocean salinity has held near its present value over long spans of time.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: The Rock Record Is Incomplete
concepts.strand: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.unit: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.topic: Rock Cycle and Earth Materials Synthesis
concepts.summary: Because recycling destroys rock, a missing rock type at an outcrop means only that it is absent there, and the oldest surviving rocks are found in stable continental interiors where burial and erosion have been least.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: The Water Budget Equation
concepts.summary: For a watershed, precipitation equals evapotranspiration plus runoff plus the change in storage, so a persistent deficit lowers the water table while a surplus raises streamflow and recharge.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Thermohaline Circulation and Climate
concepts.summary: Cold salty water sinking in the North Atlantic drives a slow overturning circulation with a timescale near a thousand years, so a large freshwater input that freshens the surface can weaken it.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Thunderstorms and Tornadoes
concepts.summary: A thunderstorm needs moisture, instability and lift, and when wind shear tilts the updraft it begins to rotate as a mesocyclone from which a tornado can descend.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Tides from Differential Gravity
concepts.summary: The Moon pulls hardest on the near side of Earth and least on the far side, producing two tidal bulges, and the Sun's alignment adds to them at new and full moon for spring tides and subtracts at the quarter phases for neap tides.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Tilt, Not Distance, Causes the Seasons
concepts.summary: Earth's axis is tilted about 23.5 degrees, so each hemisphere receives more direct sunlight over longer days for half the year, which is why the two hemispheres have opposite seasons even though Earth is nearest the Sun in January.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Transform Boundaries and Lateral Faulting
concepts.summary: Plates sliding past each other produce shallow earthquakes along a transform fault and no volcanism, because no lithosphere is created or destroyed at that boundary.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Triangulation Locates an Epicenter
concepts.summary: The P-to-S arrival gap grows with distance from the focus, so converting that gap to a distance at three stations and drawing three circles fixes the epicenter at their single intersection.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Tropical Cyclones: Requirements and Hazards
concepts.summary: A tropical cyclone needs ocean water warmer than about 26 degrees Celsius, low wind shear and enough Coriolis effect to organise, which is why none forms at the equator, and it weakens once it moves over land.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Tsunamis and Their Warning
concepts.summary: A megathrust rupture or submarine landslide displaces the water column, and the resulting wave is low and fast in open ocean but slows and steepens in shallow water, so warning depends on fast seismic detection and deep-ocean pressure buoys.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Two Energy Engines: Sun and Interior
concepts.strand: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.unit: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.summary: Solar radiation drives the atmosphere, ocean and water cycle from outside while radioactive decay and residual heat of accretion drive tectonics from inside, so a landscape records both surface and interior processes at once.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Types and Triggers of Mass Movement
concepts.summary: Creep is slow, a slump rotates, a debris flow is fast and water-rich and a rockfall is free fall, and heavy rain, earthquakes and vegetation removal trigger them by raising load or lowering strength.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Uncertainty, Replication, and Peer Review
concepts.strand: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.unit: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.summary: Every measurement carries a stated uncertainty range, so a conclusion is accepted only when independent measurements agree within those ranges and another worker can reproduce the result.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Unconformities Record Missing Time
concepts.strand: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.unit: Geologic Time, Earth History, and Life
concepts.summary: An angular unconformity is a tilted eroded sequence buried by flat layers, a disconformity is an erosion surface between parallel beds and a nonconformity is one cut into igneous or metamorphic rock, so each marks a gap rather than continuous deposition.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Unintended Consequences and Adaptive Management
concepts.summary: A dam that traps sediment starves the delta downstream and accelerates coastal retreat, so a large Earth work needs monitoring and adjustment rather than a one-time approval.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Unit Conversion and Scientific Notation
concepts.strand: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.unit: Earth Science Practices and Reference Tools
concepts.topic: Reference Tables, Units, and Formula Tools
concepts.summary: A unit is converted by multiplying by a ratio equal to one, as one kilometre over one thousand metres does, so 3,500 metres becomes 3.5 kilometres, and very large or small quantities are written as powers of ten.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Upwelling and Coastal Productivity
concepts.summary: Wind blowing along a coast moves surface water offshore so deeper nutrient-rich water rises to replace it, which is why coastal upwelling zones support the most productive fisheries.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Wave Refraction and Longshore Drift
concepts.summary: Waves refract until they meet the shore nearly head-on and the resulting longshore current carries sand along the beach, so a groin traps sand on its updrift side and starves the beach downdrift.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: What Makes a Mineral
concepts.strand: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.unit: Minerals, Rocks, and the Rock Cycle
concepts.summary: A mineral is naturally occurring, inorganic, solid, has a definite chemical composition and an ordered crystal structure, which is why glass lacks the structure and coal lacks both the composition and the inorganic origin.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: When Slopes Fail
concepts.summary: Water adds weight and raises pore pressure while undercutting a slope removes its toe support, so a slope fails when the driving stress exceeds the shear strength of its material.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Which Ice Raises Sea Level
concepts.summary: Floating sea ice already displaces its own weight so melting it leaves sea level unchanged, whereas loss from a land-based ice sheet adds new water to the ocean, so Greenland and Antarctica set the rate of sea-level rise.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Why Plates Move at Different Speeds
concepts.summary: A plate's speed reflects the balance between its driving forces and the resistance it meets, so a plate with long subducting margins such as the Pacific moves several times faster than one bordered largely by continental collision.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence

concepts.title: Wind Erosion and Deposition
concepts.summary: Wind sorts fine material and abrades rock, building dunes whose cross-beds dip downwind and blanketing distant ground with loess, so wind deposits are well sorted and fine grained.

provenance.source: Earth and Space Science - Systems, Cycles and Evidence
